scopeAuthority.rule: Core questions must map to an Advanced knowledge topic/objective. CARs Part IX/other CARs provide legal authority; TC AIM/NAV CANADA/ISED provide supporting operational material where applicable.

questions.question: A Transport Canada inspector asks an RPAS pilot to produce an aviation document that the pilot is required to hold. Which response best reflects the CARs compliance framework?
choices: The pilot may refuse unless police are present.
The pilot must produce the required aviation document when lawfully requested.
Only paper originals may ever be produced.
The request applies only to crewed-aircraft pilots.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to know who may demand inspection of aviation documents and the associated compliance obligations
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CARs Part I — inspection and production of aviation documents
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to know who may demand inspection of aviation documents and the associated compliance obligations.

questions.question: A company stores required aviation records electronically instead of on paper. Which principle does TP 15263 expect an Advanced pilot to understand?
choices: Electronic records are never acceptable.
Computer-stored records may be used when appropriate measures protect their integrity and availability.
Electronic records are valid only for 30 days.
Only NAV CANADA may authorize electronic records.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 explicitly includes the principle that computer-stored records may replace paper records when protective measures are taken
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CARs Part I — record keeping and electronic records
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 explicitly includes the principle that computer-stored records may replace paper records when protective measures are taken.

questions.question: A pilot wants to conduct an RPAS operation entirely inside a warehouse. Which regulatory-scope concept should be checked first?
choices: Whether Part IX applies to indoor operations at all.
Whether the warehouse is inside Class G airspace.
Whether the roof height exceeds 400 ft.
Whether the pilot has filed a NOTAM.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to know the CARs application rule concerning indoor and underground operations
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CARs Part I — application to indoor or underground operations
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to know the CARs application rule concerning indoor and underground operations.

questions.question: An RPA is flying normally, but a developing failure makes continued flight likely to endanger persons on the ground. Before using a flight-termination function, what must the pilot consider under CAR 901.44?
choices: Whether activation itself will or is likely to endanger aviation safety or any person.
Whether the aircraft is below 400 ft AGL only.
Whether the visual observer agrees in writing.
Whether the aircraft has flown for at least five minutes.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.44 prohibits activation of a flight-termination system when doing so will or is likely to endanger aviation safety or any person
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: A pilot proposes installing an emergency locator transmitter (ELT) on an RPA as a precaution. Which statement reflects CAR 901.45?
choices: An ELT is mandatory on every Advanced RPA.
An RPA must not be equipped with an ELT.
An ELT is required only at night.
An ELT may be installed if the pilot holds a ROC-A.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.45 prohibits operating an RPA equipped with an emergency locator transmitter
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: A planned operation falls outside the ordinary operating privileges available under Part IX. What regulatory mechanism should the pilot consider?
choices: A Special Flight Operations Certificate — RPAS, where required by Subpart 903.
A recreational pilot permit.
A VFR flight itinerary only.
A municipal business licence as a substitute for aviation authorization.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to give examples of operations requiring an SFOC-RPAS and understand the Subpart 903 pathway
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to give examples of operations requiring an SFOC-RPAS and understand the Subpart 903 pathway.

questions.question: A pilot plans an RPA flight at an advertised public event. Which initial regulatory question is most important?
choices: Whether CAR 901.41 requires an SFOC-RPAS for the proposed operation or whether a specific exception applies.
Whether the event has food vendors.
Whether the pilot can remain below 50 ft AGL.
Whether the RPA has obstacle avoidance.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.41 makes advertised-event operations an SFOC-RPAS issue unless an applicable exception is satisfied
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an RPA from an RPAS for regulatory study purposes?
choices: The RPA is the aircraft; the RPAS includes the aircraft and associated elements required for operation such as the control station and C2 link.
RPA and RPAS always mean exactly the same physical object.
RPAS means only the control station.
RPA means only an aircraft heavier than 25 kg.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to define remotely piloted aircraft, remotely piloted aircraft system, control station and command-and-control link
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: CARs terminology — RPA, RPAS, C2 link and control station
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to define remotely piloted aircraft, remotely piloted aircraft system, control station and command-and-control link.

questions.question: A pilot identifies an active CYR area on the planned route. What is the correct starting assumption?
choices: Entry is permitted below 400 ft AGL.
Authorization from the person or agency specified for the restricted area is required before entry.
An Advanced certificate automatically authorizes entry.
CYR areas apply only to IFR aircraft.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to recall that operations in Class F restricted airspace require authorization from the person specified in the DAH
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to recall that operations in Class F restricted airspace require authorization from the person specified in the DAH.
questions.source: CAR 601.04; NAV CANADA DAH; TP 15263 Section 1

questions.question: A CYA advisory area is published along the route. Which statement is most accurate?
choices: CYA means entry is legally prohibited in all circumstances.
The pilot must determine the area's activity, hazards and current status; advisory designation is not the same as restricted airspace.
CYA automatically becomes Class G whenever no NOTAM is issued.
CYA areas can be ignored by RPAS below 400 ft.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires operational understanding of Class F special-use airspace and the DAH; advisory and restricted designations must not be confused
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: Class F advisory airspace — operational assessment
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires operational understanding of Class F special-use airspace and the DAH; advisory and restricted designations must not be confused.

questions.question: An Advanced pilot receives authorization to operate in Class D controlled airspace. What remains true?
choices: The authorization eliminates all other Part IX requirements.
The pilot must comply with ATC instructions and the conditions of the authorization in addition to other applicable requirements.
The pilot may disregard later ATC instructions if they differ from the original authorization.
The authorization converts the airspace to Class G for the RPA.
questions.rationale: Advanced controlled-airspace operations require authorization and compliance with ATC instructions; authorization does not displace other applicable rules
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: Controlled airspace — ATS authorization and ATC instructions
questions.learningObjective: Advanced controlled-airspace operations require authorization and compliance with ATC instructions; authorization does not displace other applicable rules.
questions.source: CAR 901.71-901.72; TC AIM RPA; TP 15263 Section 1

questions.question: Why must a pilot distinguish an aerodrome's proximity rules from the classification of the surrounding airspace?
choices: Because aerodrome-proximity requirements and controlled-airspace requirements are separate regulatory questions that can apply independently.
Because every aerodrome is surrounded by Class C airspace.
Because uncontrolled airspace removes all aerodrome rules.
Because an Advanced certificate replaces both requirements.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 separately requires knowledge of airspace classification and operations at or near aerodromes; one determination does not answer the other
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 separately requires knowledge of airspace classification and operations at or near aerodromes; one determination does not answer the other.

questions.question: A wildfire is being actively fought by aircraft. What should an RPAS pilot understand about the associated forest-fire airspace restriction?
choices: RPAS may enter if they stay under 400 ft AGL.
Aircraft operations near a forest fire are subject to specific CAR restrictions intended to protect fire-control aircraft and operations.
Only helicopters are restricted.
The restriction applies only when a control tower is open.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 explicitly requires recall of restrictions on all aircraft, including RPA, in the vicinity of forest-fire areas
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 explicitly requires recall of restrictions on all aircraft, including RPA, in the vicinity of forest-fire areas.

questions.question: A pilot is operating in transponder airspace with an RPA that lacks the normally required equipment. When can an exception be considered under CAR 901.46?
choices: Whenever the RPA remains in VLOS.
When the responsible ATC unit provides service, authorization is requested before entry, and aviation safety is not likely to be affected.
Whenever an Advanced certificate is held.
Only after entering the airspace.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.46 provides a specific pre-entry ATC authorization pathway for an unequipped RPA; VLOS or certificate level alone does not create the exception
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: What is the practical purpose of identifying whether a planned operation lies in an altimeter-setting region or standard-pressure region?
choices: It determines the pressure reference used for altitude reporting and interpretation in the applicable airspace.
It determines whether the RPA must be painted a specific colour.
It automatically determines the pilot-certificate level.
It replaces the need to check the DAH.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to identify the altimeter-setting region and standard-pressure region as part of airspace knowledge
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to identify the altimeter-setting region and standard-pressure region as part of airspace knowledge.

questions.question: An uncontrolled RPA inadvertently enters controlled airspace. What should the pilot's response be based on?
choices: The applicable inadvertent-entry and emergency procedures, including communication/notification as required, rather than continuing as planned.
The assumption that controlled airspace rules no longer apply after accidental entry.
A rule requiring immediate battery shutdown in every case.
A requirement to climb above 400 ft.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 includes inadvertent entry into controlled airspace and emergency procedures as Advanced knowledge topics
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 includes inadvertent entry into controlled airspace and emergency procedures as Advanced knowledge topics.

questions.question: A VLOS operation is planned 2.8 NM from an airport centre. What additional airport-specific condition must be checked under the Advanced Operations division?
choices: Whether the operation can be conducted in accordance with the established RPAS procedure applicable to that airport.
Whether the RPA is painted orange.
Whether the flight lasts less than 10 minutes.
Whether the pilot can avoid using GPS.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.73 requires a Division V operation less than 3 NM from an airport centre to follow the established RPAS procedure applicable to that airport
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.
questions.source: CAR 901.73; TC AIM RPA; TP 15263 Section 1

questions.question: A VLOS operation is planned exactly 1.0 NM from the centre of a heliport. Which wording detail matters when applying the ordinary heliport-distance trigger?
choices: The rule uses 'less than 1 NM', so exactly 1.0 NM is not inside that particular numerical trigger, although other aerodrome and airspace rules still apply.
The rule means 1 NM or less.
Exactly 1 NM always requires an SFOC-RPAS.
Distance is irrelevant at heliports.
questions.rationale: Advanced exam questions can hinge on exclusive regulatory wording; the less-than-1-NM heliport trigger does not include exactly 1.0 NM
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Advanced exam questions can hinge on exclusive regulatory wording; the less-than-1-NM heliport trigger does not include exactly 1.

questions.question: An RPA is outside the 3 NM airport-distance trigger but would cross an active downwind leg used by crewed aircraft. What is the key concern?
choices: CAR 901.47 traffic-pattern interference remains relevant even outside the numerical distance trigger.
The RPA has priority because it is farther than 3 NM from the airport centre.
No aerodrome rule can apply outside 3 NM.
Only the airport manager can determine collision risk.
questions.rationale: The traffic-pattern interference prohibition is an independent requirement and is not switched off merely because a numerical distance threshold is not triggered
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: The traffic-pattern interference prohibition is an independent requirement and is not switched off merely because a numerical distance threshold is not triggered.

questions.question: A pilot wants to operate on the movement area of a certified airport. Which approvals must be considered?
choices: Approval/control requirements of the airport or aerodrome operator and the appropriate ATS unit, as applicable.
Only permission from a nearby property owner.
Only a Basic pilot certificate.
No approval if the RPA is under 250 g.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to understand that persons, vehicles, obstacles and operations at aerodromes are subject to operator and appropriate ATC control/approval
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to understand that persons, vehicles, obstacles and operations at aerodromes are subject to operator and appropriate ATC control/approval.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled aerodrome, why is understanding the normal circuit and taxi flow important to an RPAS pilot?
choices: It helps predict where crewed aircraft may be operating so the RPA can avoid interference and collision risk.
It allows the RPA to join the circuit as an aircraft with priority.
It removes the need for a site survey.
It determines battery capacity.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 Flight Operations requires pilots to describe the normal flow of traditional aircraft traffic at an aerodrome, including circuit and taxiing activity
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 Flight Operations requires pilots to describe the normal flow of traditional aircraft traffic at an aerodrome, including circuit and taxiing activity.

questions.question: What is the main operational distinction between an MF area and an aerodrome traffic frequency (ATF) environment?
choices: An MF area has mandatory frequency procedures; an ATF supports traffic coordination where the applicable published procedures differ.
ATF always provides radar separation.
MF is used only by helicopters.
There is no operational distinction.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to understand controlled and uncontrolled aerodrome operations, MF and ATF procedures
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: Mandatory Frequency and Aerodrome Traffic Frequency procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires Advanced pilots to understand controlled and uncontrolled aerodrome operations, MF and ATF procedures.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 1; TC AIM RAC; NAV CANADA VFR Phraseology Guide

questions.question: A VLOS operation is planned 2.5 NM from the centre of an aerodrome operated under the authority of the Minister of National Defence. What specific authorization is required?
choices: Authorization from the Department of National Defence.
Only an airport operator's civilian RPAS procedure.
Only an Advanced certificate.
None if the airspace is uncontrolled.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.47(4) separately requires DND authorization for operations less than 3 NM from a DND aerodrome
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes an aerodrome from an airport in Canadian aviation law?
choices: An airport is an aerodrome for which an airport certificate is in force; not every aerodrome is a certified airport.
Every aerodrome is automatically an airport.
An airport is any place where an RPA launches.
Aerodrome is a NAV CANADA term with no legal meaning.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to define aerodrome and airport and understand the different regulatory treatment of aerodromes and certified airports
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to define aerodrome and airport and understand the different regulatory treatment of aerodromes and certified airports.

questions.question: In an ICAO NOTAM Q-code, what do the four letters after the initial Q primarily describe?
choices: The subject and its condition/status.
The pilot certificate required.
The exact latitude and longitude only.
The issuing airport's runway length.
questions.rationale: Canadian NOTAM interpretation uses the Q-code subject and condition to classify the aeronautical information
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Canadian NOTAM interpretation uses the Q-code subject and condition to classify the aeronautical information.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 1; NAV CANADA NOTAM procedures

questions.question: A NOTAM Q-line shows a broad radius, while Item E contains precise polygon coordinates for the affected activity. Which information should be treated as the more precise operational geometry?
choices: The detailed Item E geometry.
The Q-line radius in every case.
A fixed 5 NM circle.
The FIR boundary.
questions.rationale: The Q-line supports filtering and area-of-influence processing; precise operational geometry described in the NOTAM text should be used when provided
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.knowledgeTopic: NOTAM Q-line filtering versus detailed geometry
questions.learningObjective: The Q-line supports filtering and area-of-influence processing; precise operational geometry described in the NOTAM text should be used when provided.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 1; NAV CANADA NOTAM procedures

questions.question: Why should a pilot not use the Q-line lower and upper vertical qualifiers as the sole source of exact operational limits?
choices: They support NOTAM filtering; the detailed NOTAM fields/text provide the actual limits that must be interpreted.
They are always expressed in metres AGL.
They apply only to IFR flights.
They are decorative metadata.
questions.rationale: Advanced NOTAM interpretation requires distinguishing Q-line filtering qualifiers from the detailed operational information in the NOTAM
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Advanced NOTAM interpretation requires distinguishing Q-line filtering qualifiers from the detailed operational information in the NOTAM.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 1; NAV CANADA NOTAM procedures

questions.question: A NOTAM is published with times in UTC. A pilot planning in Eastern Time should do what?
choices: Convert the published UTC validity period carefully to the local operating time and account for the correct UTC offset.
Assume NOTAM times are always local.
Subtract 12 hours in every season.
Ignore the time if the NOTAM is within the same FIR.
questions.rationale: Operational NOTAM planning requires correct interpretation of published UTC validity periods relative to the planned local operation
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Operational NOTAM planning requires correct interpretation of published UTC validity periods relative to the planned local operation.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 1; NAV CANADA NOTAM procedures

questions.question: A NOTAM is cancelled before the planned flight. What should the pilot conclude?
choices: The cancelled notice is no longer current, but the pilot must still check for replacement or newly issued information affecting the operation.
The original restriction permanently remains in force.
All NOTAMs for the FIR are cancelled.
No further pre-flight information check is required.
questions.rationale: NOTAM status must be assessed using current information; cancellation of one notice does not guarantee that no replacement or related notice exists
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: NOTAM status must be assessed using current information; cancellation of one notice does not guarantee that no replacement or related notice exists.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 1; NAV CANADA NOTAM procedures

questions.question: During the site survey, why should the pilot review both aerodrome-specific and area/FIR NOTAM information where relevant?
choices: Hazards affecting the operation may be published under different NOTAM locations or scopes, so a single aerodrome search may not capture everything.
FIR NOTAMs never apply below 400 ft.
Aerodrome NOTAMs replace all area information.
Only NOTAMs containing 'RPAS' can affect an RPAS operation.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 and CAR site-survey/pre-flight requirements require pilots to obtain current aeronautical information relevant to the operation
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 and CAR site-survey/pre-flight requirements require pilots to obtain current aeronautical information relevant to the operation.
questions.source: CAR 901.27; TP 15263 Section 1; NAV CANADA NOTAM procedures

questions.question: A NOTAM warns of crane activity near the planned operating area. What is the correct use of that information?
choices: Incorporate the obstacle location/height and validity period into the site survey and operational-volume planning.
Ignore it if the crane is outside airport property.
Assume the crane lights guarantee separation.
Treat the NOTAM as applicable only to crewed aircraft.
questions.rationale: NOTAM obstacle information is operational aeronautical information that must be considered when assessing obstacles and the planned flight path
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.knowledgeTopic: NOTAM obstacle information in site survey
questions.learningObjective: NOTAM obstacle information is operational aeronautical information that must be considered when assessing obstacles and the planned flight path.

questions.question: A forest-fire NOTAM is issued for an area. Which statement is correct?
choices: The pilot must consider both the NOTAM and the underlying CAR forest-fire operating restrictions; the NOTAM does not replace the regulation.
The NOTAM creates an exemption for Advanced pilots.
Only the NOTAM matters; CAR 601.15 can be ignored.
The restriction ends automatically when the pilot can no longer see smoke.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires knowledge of forest-fire operating restrictions and related NOTAM information as complementary sources
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires knowledge of forest-fire operating restrictions and related NOTAM information as complementary sources.

questions.question: A METAR shows temperature and dew point rapidly converging toward the same value while winds are light. What hazard should receive increased attention?
choices: Fog or low-cloud formation and reduced visibility.
Guaranteed improvement to unlimited visibility.
A magnetic compass failure.
A transponder malfunction.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 meteorology requires understanding humidity, dew point, visibility and cloud/fog formation for operational decisions
questions.knowledgeArea: Meteorology
questions.knowledgeTopic: Humidity, dew point and fog formation
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 meteorology requires understanding humidity, dew point, visibility and cloud/fog formation for operational decisions.

questions.question: A strong wind crosses a ridge before reaching the operating site on the lee side. What should the pilot anticipate?
choices: Mechanical turbulence, rotor effects and potentially large local wind variations.
Perfectly smooth air because the ridge blocks the wind.
No wind at ground level.
Only a change in GNSS accuracy.
questions.rationale: Topography can create mechanical turbulence and significant local wind effects that must be considered in RPAS planning
questions.knowledgeArea: Meteorology
questions.learningObjective: Topography can create mechanical turbulence and significant local wind effects that must be considered in RPAS planning.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a METAR and a TAF for pre-flight planning?
choices: A METAR reports observed aerodrome weather; a TAF provides a forecast for the aerodrome and validity period.
A TAF is an aircraft maintenance report.
A METAR is always a 24-hour forecast.
They are identical products.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to interpret aviation weather reports and aerodrome forecasts as different products
questions.knowledgeArea: Meteorology
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to interpret aviation weather reports and aerodrome forecasts as different products.

questions.question: A cold front is approaching the operating area. Which weather tendency is generally most relevant to an RPAS pilot?
choices: Potential rapid changes in wind, turbulence, cloud and precipitation near frontal passage.
Guaranteed calm winds and clear skies.
No change in pressure or temperature.
A permanent increase in GNSS accuracy.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires understanding frontal weather and how pressure systems and air masses affect operational conditions
questions.knowledgeArea: Meteorology
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires understanding frontal weather and how pressure systems and air masses affect operational conditions.

questions.question: Why can a high density altitude reduce RPAS performance margin?
choices: Lower air density can reduce aerodynamic and propulsion effectiveness, affecting climb, payload and endurance margins.
It makes the aircraft heavier on a scale.
It increases battery voltage automatically.
It removes wind effects.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to assess density altitude for anticipated performance and flight-envelope limitations
questions.knowledgeArea: Meteorology
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to assess density altitude for anticipated performance and flight-envelope limitations.

questions.question: Thunderstorms are forecast near the operating area. Which planning decision best reflects TP 15263 knowledge requirements?
choices: Maintain conservative separation and account for strong gusts, turbulence, precipitation and rapid wind shifts rather than planning to operate underneath the cell.
Operate directly below the cloud because the RPA remains under 400 ft.
Use obstacle avoidance as a thunderstorm-detection system.
Assume small RPA are unaffected by convective outflows.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 Flight Operations explicitly includes thunderstorm avoidance and Meteorology covers convective hazards
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 Flight Operations explicitly includes thunderstorm avoidance and Meteorology covers convective hazards.
questions.source: TP 15263 Sections 4 and 6; TC AIM MET

questions.question: Icing is reported along the intended route. What is the regulatory decision point under CAR 901.35?
choices: Do not operate unless the applicable icing provisions are satisfied, including the required de-icing/anti-icing equipment or a means to detect icing where the exception applies.
Continue if the aircraft is under 25 kg.
Continue if the pilot can see the propellers.
Icing rules apply only above 400 ft AGL.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.35 establishes specific restrictions on operation in icing conditions and on contamination of critical surfaces
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: A deepening low-pressure system is moving toward the mission area. Which broad expectation is most useful for planning?
choices: Weather may become more unsettled, with changing winds/cloud/precipitation, so current forecasts and observations should be reassessed.
Low pressure guarantees calm clear weather.
Pressure systems do not affect RPAS operations.
Only temperature changes; wind cannot change.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to relate weather characteristics and air movement to high- and low-pressure systems
questions.knowledgeArea: Meteorology
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to relate weather characteristics and air movement to high- and low-pressure systems.

questions.question: A visual observer detects a helicopter approaching the operating area but cannot communicate promptly with the pilot. What crew requirement has failed?
choices: The ability to maintain reliable and timely communication needed to support the operation.
The requirement to carry an ELT.
The requirement to use a transponder.
The requirement to file an IFR flight plan.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 and Part IX visual-observer requirements depend on effective crew communication so hazards can be acted upon
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.knowledgeTopic: Visual observer — reliable and timely communication
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 and Part IX visual-observer requirements depend on effective crew communication so hazards can be acted upon.

questions.question: During a VLOS operation, who may maintain the required visual line of sight with the RPA?
choices: The pilot or a properly used visual observer, subject to the applicable VLOS requirements.
Only the pilot; a visual observer can never satisfy VLOS.
Only an ATC controller.
Any member of the public.
questions.rationale: Part IX VLOS provisions permit the required visual line of sight to be maintained by the pilot or a properly used visual observer
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: Part IX VLOS provisions permit the required visual line of sight to be maintained by the pilot or a properly used visual observer.

questions.question: For an EVLOS operation under Division V, what must the visual observer watch?
choices: The operating airspace sufficiently to detect conflicting traffic and other hazards and enable avoidance action.
Only the live camera feed.
Only the pilot's hands.
Only the RPA battery percentage.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.74 requires the EVLOS visual observer to maintain unaided visual contact with the operating airspace to detect conflicts and hazards
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: An EVLOS observer is 2.1 NM from the RPA while all other conditions are satisfied. Which statement is correct?
choices: The operation does not satisfy the ordinary EVLOS distance condition requiring the RPA to remain no more than 2 NM from the required persons/control station.
The operation is compliant because 2 NM is only a recommendation.
The observer may be any distance away if binoculars are used.
Distance matters only in controlled airspace.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.74 contains a no-more-than-2-NM condition for the RPA relative to the pilot, control station and visual observer
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: Which qualification can satisfy the certificate requirement for a visual observer supporting an EVLOS operation under CAR 901.75?
choices: A Basic, Advanced, or Level 1 Complex RPAS pilot certificate, provided the other observer conditions are met.
No aviation qualification of any kind.
Only an airline transport pilot licence.
Only an Advanced RPAS certificate.
questions.rationale: CAR 901.75 identifies acceptable RPAS pilot certificates for an EVLOS visual observer and imposes additional visual-contact/distance requirements
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: CAR 901.

questions.question: A visual observer becomes occupied with a phone call and stops scanning the operating airspace. What is the primary operational problem?
choices: The observer can no longer reliably perform the assigned collision/hazard-detection function.
The phone automatically invalidates the RPA registration.
The pilot must switch to IFR.
The RPA must immediately climb.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 emphasizes attention management, situational awareness and visual-observer responsibilities during RPAS operations
questions.knowledgeArea: Human factors
questions.knowledgeTopic: Visual observer attention and situational awareness
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 emphasizes attention management, situational awareness and visual-observer responsibilities during RPAS operations.

questions.question: Before launch, what should the pilot and visual observer agree on to reduce ambiguity during a traffic conflict?
choices: Clear communication terms, responsibilities and immediate actions for reporting and avoiding conflicting aircraft.
A plan to discuss responsibilities only after takeoff.
A rule that the observer never interrupts the pilot.
A requirement to use text messages for every warning.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires crew communication, planning, responsibilities and collision-avoidance coordination as part of Advanced operations
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires crew communication, planning, responsibilities and collision-avoidance coordination as part of Advanced operations.

questions.question: A visual observer can see the RPA only through a zoomed video display and cannot visually scan the surrounding operating airspace. Why is that insufficient for an EVLOS observer?
choices: EVLOS observer duties require unaided visual contact with the operating airspace sufficient to detect conflicting traffic and hazards.
A video display is legally identical to unaided visual contact.
The observer's only duty is to monitor battery voltage.
EVLOS does not require traffic detection.

questions.question: A pilot is given a bearing to a landmark. What does bearing describe?
choices: The direction from one point to another relative to a stated reference.
The aircraft's mass.
The vertical speed.
The battery temperature.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 lists bearing as a navigation definition requiring operational understanding
questions.knowledgeArea: Navigation
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 lists bearing as a navigation definition requiring operational understanding.

questions.question: Wildlife begins reacting strongly to the RPA near a nesting area. What is the best operational response?
choices: Increase separation or terminate/relocate the operation to avoid creating a wildlife hazard or disturbance.
Fly closer to document the reaction.
Use louder propellers.
Assume wildlife concerns are unrelated to flight safety.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 Flight Operations explicitly includes wildlife hazards and wildlife conservation
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 Flight Operations explicitly includes wildlife hazards and wildlife conservation.

questions.question: Why is launching near active fire-control aircraft especially hazardous?
choices: An RPA can conflict with low-flying firefighting aircraft and disrupt emergency operations, which is why specific forest-fire restrictions exist.
Firefighting aircraft always fly above 10,000 ft.
RPA have automatic priority near emergencies.
Smoke guarantees visual separation.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires pilots to know forest-fire restrictions and the safety rationale for protecting fire-control aircraft
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires pilots to know forest-fire restrictions and the safety rationale for protecting fire-control aircraft.

questions.question: A high-power laser display is planned near the operating area. Why should the pilot investigate it?
choices: Directed bright light can create an aviation hazard and is subject to specific Canadian aviation restrictions/notification requirements.
Lasers improve visual-observer performance.
Laser activity automatically closes all Class G airspace.
Only military aircraft are affected.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 includes restrictions and notification requirements for projection of directed bright light sources at aircraft
questions.knowledgeArea: Air law, air traffic rules and procedures
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 includes restrictions and notification requirements for projection of directed bright light sources at aircraft.

questions.question: A night mission is legal and the RPA lights are operating. Why should the pilot still assess the effect of those lights on other people or aircraft?
choices: Required lighting supports conspicuity but can also create glare/distraction depending on orientation and environment; operational risk still must be managed.
Legal lights eliminate every other risk.
Brighter is always safer regardless of direction.
Lights matter only to photographers.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 includes collision avoidance/use of lights and broader operational risk assessment
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 includes collision avoidance/use of lights and broader operational risk assessment.

questions.question: A crowd begins forming near the planned launch point after the site survey was completed. What should the pilot do?
choices: Reassess the site and person-exposure controls before launch; the earlier survey does not freeze conditions in time.
Launch because the site survey was already signed.
Ask the crowd to watch the RPA for traffic.
Ignore the change if the weather is unchanged.
questions.rationale: A site survey and operational risk assessment must remain representative of actual conditions at the time of flight
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: A site survey and operational risk assessment must remain representative of actual conditions at the time of flight.

questions.question: Why should a pilot establish a clear abort criterion before a complex mission?
choices: Predefined limits reduce pressure to continue when safety margins deteriorate and support consistent decision-making.
Abort criteria remove the need for pilot judgment.
They allow regulatory limits to be exceeded once.
They are useful only for crewed aircraft.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 Human Factors and Flight Operations require risk management, sound decision-making and emergency/contingency planning
questions.knowledgeArea: Human factors
questions.knowledgeTopic: Operational risk limits and abort criteria
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 Human Factors and Flight Operations require risk management, sound decision-making and emergency/contingency planning.

questions.question: A bird is circling aggressively near the RPA. What is the safest immediate principle?
choices: Increase separation and recover the RPA if necessary rather than escalating the encounter.
Chase the bird away with the RPA.
Climb directly above the bird.
Remain stationary until the bird contacts the aircraft.
questions.rationale: Wildlife hazards can threaten both the aircraft and wildlife; TP 15263 requires recognition and mitigation of these risks
questions.knowledgeArea: Flight operations
questions.learningObjective: Wildlife hazards can threaten both the aircraft and wildlife; TP 15263 requires recognition and mitigation of these risks.

questions.question: A pilot identifies a hazard whose probability is low but whose consequence could be catastrophic. How should that influence planning?
choices: The severity still warrants meaningful controls; low probability alone does not justify ignoring a catastrophic consequence.
Ignore it because low-probability hazards never matter.
Accept it automatically if the flight is under 400 ft.
Transfer responsibility to the visual observer.
questions.rationale: TP 15263 requires risk-management thinking that considers both likelihood and consequence when deciding whether an operation is acceptable
questions.knowledgeArea: Human factors
questions.learningObjective: TP 15263 requires risk-management thinking that considers both likelihood and consequence when deciding whether an operation is acceptable.
